In the USA, the withdrawals of LME material have slowed, as have those from Comex warehouses. - Demand for refined copper in China and Europe remains subdued, while in the USA it appears to be holding up relatively well. On the other hand, refined production growth continues to be modest. This is leaving the spot market to react to shifts in the availability of exchange and Chinese bonded stocks. - The price has come under pressure due to the combination of the unwinding of the backwardation and the potential for Greece to leave the Eurozone and, more recently, the threat of Spanish banks opening another chapter in the saga of the single currency. |The supply/demand

The price decline was due to the latest developments in the Eurozone crisis, with Greece likely to leave the euro and, more recently, fears that troubles at Spanish banks could open a new and more dangerous chapter in the single currency’s saga. In addition, the latest slide in the price followed the widest backwardation (cash to 3-m) on the LME since just before the global financial crisis started. The backwardation had resulted from a short covering rally in the wake of the largest ever one-day cancellation of warrants on the LME. irst half of the month as more metal was delivered into LME warehouses. At the time of writing the back had narrowed to almost nothing. The market rumours were that the cancellation was the work of one large trader who was squeezing short positions held mainly by Chinese smelters, several of which made an announcement that they would make a concerted effort to deliver metal to the LME to help rebalance the market. #### …due mainly to Chinese exports of surplus cathode… In addition to the efforts of the Chinese smelters, over the past month we have been told by most market participants that there has been an increase in exports from China from bonded warehouses. The volume of metal in these warehouses fell from a high of approximately 650,000t in mid-May to around 615,000t at the end of the month. This is in response to the backwardation on the LME, holders of stock in China can export it and benefit from selling at the higher LME price, but also because of the backwardation they can benefit from lending the metal to the LME market (sell for cash price and simultaneously buy it back at the lower 3-month price) if they will require it later. Refined exports rose slightly to 27,420t in April, from 26,537t in March and up massively from only 700t in February. Chinese market participants believe that exports in May will be 20,000t higher, which looks plausible given the marked increase in LME Asia warehouse stocks. Open tonnage (total tonnage less material for which the warrant has been cancelled) in Asian warehouses has risen by over 37,000t so far in May. We believe that the official Chinese exports for May will report a total refined import figure well © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 18 Copper Monitor June 2012 www. crugroup.com above 30,000t. Most of the rise, which has more than tripled the level of open tonnage in the region from the 16,400t recorded on 3rd May, has been in the South Korean warehouses that are nearest to China. #### …with Chinese refined imports and production down… In China, the physical market is beginning to rebalance following the large rise in stocks that reached a peak last month. In part this was the result of reduced imports. In April, Chinese refined imports amounted to only 272,903t, down from 345,667t in March, and we anticipate that May imports will fall further, possibly below the 200,000t level that is the monthly average required to make up the difference between Chinese domestic refined production and consumption. The opposite movements in Chinese import and export levels resulted in a 130,000t reduction in net imports in April compared to February. Scrap imports also fell, though less dramatically, to 370,919t gross weight in April from 430,076t in March. The reduction in net imports has resulted, as already noted Jan/2008 Jan/2009 Jan/2010 Jan/2011 above, in a lowering of bonded warehouse stocks. In Data: GTIS, CRU addition, cathode inventory drawdowns in SHFE warehouses accelerated throughout May, falling by over 17,000t in the first two weeks of the month and by almost 30,000t in H2, taking stocks down to 157,489t. The decline over the latter half of the month was the highest two-week decrease since May last year. #### …narrowing the SHFE/LME arbitrage As the price fell below RMB57,000/t on SHFE, mainly in response to the lower LME price but also to the weak domestic demand picture, the backwardation between the 3-month price and the cash-month price widened to average over RMB600/t over the past two weeks. This compares to an average differential of just under RMB100/t in the preceding period, as the increased exports to feed the LME squeeze saw increased demand for nearby metal in China. The firmer SHFE price and weaker LME price has narrowed the arbitrage between the two exchanges to less than $100/t from over $500/t at its recent widest point at the end of April. However, this narrowing is not yet translating into much of an increase in the premium on imported cathode in China, which remains at a low level of around $50/t. #### LME/Comex arbitrage widens In addition to the narrowing of the SHFE/LME negative arbitrage, the positive arbitrage between the LME and Comex has widened to an average of 3.5¢/lb in May (up to the 29th ) from 2.7¢/lb in April and © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 18 Copper Monitor June 2012 www.crugroup.com an average negative arbitrage of 1.7¢/lb in Q1 2012. The move back into a positive arbitrage comes after the high level of cancelled warrants that started in December 2011 in LME warehouses in the USA. This produced queues for metal to be delivered out and prompted traders to switch to secure metal from Comex warehouses, thus bidding up the Comex price relative to the LME. The switch back to a positive LME/Comex arbitrage indicates that this process has run its course. The traders have taken over 14,000t of copper out of Comex in May and over 27,000t since 25th January on a cumulative basis. The rate of decline has slowed to only 340t/d in the week 22nd to 29th May from 897t/d in the preceding three week period back to the beginning of May. This physical scarcity of metal compared to demand in the USA has translated into higher cathode premia. Lack of LME metal in the USA

The premium for LME grade A delivered East Coast has risen by a cent to 6.5-7.5¢/lb. Consumption has improved somewhat due to seasonally higher end-use activity. However, the main reason for the rise in premia has been tighter supply, which was exacerbated by the maintenance closure of Rio Tinto’s Kennecott smelter-refinery in Utah for 24 days, beginning 30th April. #### European consumption outlook worsens The stock movements in LME warehouses have had similar though less extreme effects on premia in Europe. The politically troubled Eurozone continues to suffer from poor sentiment. In addition, this is translating into poor demand at semis plants, which are seeing a slower than usual seasonal uptick in consumption of copper. We now forecast that Q2 refined consumption in Western Europe will be up 1.5% y-o-y. However, this result is only “strong” because of comparison to a weaker than usual Q2 in 2011. While demand is down, supply is also tight. Regional production is expected to rise by only 4,000t on Q1 to 484,000t. In addition, the mass cancellation of warrants on 20th April hit Europe, taking 19,150t out of the warehouses between 19th April and 28th May, which more than halved LME tonnage in the region to just 18,025t. As a result, the tighter supply and weaker demand are offsetting one another and premia for physical metal have remained elevated at around $75-100/t. #### Mine disruptions continue Following updates of most global mine production, we have slightly raised refined copper output for 2011 by 96,000t, mainly in H2. Our refined estimate for Q1 2011 has been maintained at output of 4.7Mt, and © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 18 Copper Monitor June 2012 www. crugroup.com a slight increase in our Q2 forecast to 4.84Mt, as the small gains in some regions outweigh the lower forecast in others. We have maintained a relatively high disruption allowance for mine production in Q2, as there have been a string of incidents across the world. These included protests in Peru over Xstrata’s Tintaya mine and Antapaccay project. There were also a couple of short strikes among the contract workers at Escondida and workers at Kazakhmys’Annensky underground copper mine in Kazakhstan. Finally, there was a twoday shut down at Collahuasi following the death of a worker in a drilling accident. The concerns about future demand for commodities generally due to the uncertain macroeconomic outlook, increased project costs and the tempering of the recovery in prices has also prompted some rethinking of projects, at least at BHP Billiton. The company has until the end of 2012 to start the expansion at Olympic Dam or lose

the permission to do so. In addition to Olympic Dam, BHP Billiton is considering a port expansion in Western Australia for iron ore and a potash project in Canada. Given changes in the economics of the various projects the company now has to decide which to go ahead with, as it does not have the capability to develop all three at once. #### Price likely to rebound from recent lows Investors have turned bearish on copper as the Greek crisis is supplanted in the headlines by fears over a potential Spanish banking crisis. This is illustrated in the chart at the right which shows the Comex nonfinancial investors moving steadily into a net short position. If a financial tsunami is triggered by the Eurozone crisis, copper prices will be under extreme pressure from fund selling, though this is not our base case yet. Having said that, the threat of a return to global economic meltdown may finally concentrates the minds of European politicians to solve the contradictions (principally the lack of fiscal union and measures such as euro bonds) at the heart of Bearish investors start going

Further bearish news comes from indications in recent press reports that China will focus stimulus efforts on investment rather than monetary policy means that the lags in this approach will not impact copper demand until later in the year and the H2 rebound may be more muted than we had been expecting. However, the modest reported stock level of 2.5 weeks of consumption means copper fundamentals are somewhat supportive of the price and will give pause to the bears to aggressively short copper. At the time of writing the next downside support level of $7,445/t is being threatened, with $7,160/t the next one after that. Barring a financial meltdown, we expect the price to find support at $7,000/t and trade in a $7,100-8,100/t range. This followed a slower start to the year as bad weather and economic fears had reduced air-conditioning demand, helping to drive a 14.5% y-o-y reduction in January’s copper tube consumption. Asia also saw increased copper tube consumption in Q1, both m-o-m and y-o-y. China and South Korea, however, both experienced declines in Q1 copper tube output, as material stocks that had begun to build last year were not draw down as expected following the Chinese New Year festival. #### European fears persist As the adjacent chart indicates, increased European q- o-q output of copper alloy RBS contributed to the quarterly global uptick, and while this was mainly due to seasonal patterns in construction activity, there were also some underlying changes at work: Construction © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 18 Copper Monitor June 2012 www. crugroup.com numbers in northern Europe have been improving mildly this year, and some of the activity that was delayed in H2 2011 due to alarm over the unfolding debt crisis could no longer be postponed and work has now begun. However, output for the quarter was down y-o-y in both copper tube and alloy RBS segments, with producers expressing doubtful sentiments. **Wieland-Werke AG** , the German fabricator of brass mill products, stated in March that demand in 2012 had begun weakly, and **KME Gro

up** of Italy was markedly dour in its Q1 report, stating that “the downward sales trend that characterized the second half of 2011 is continuing and projections provide no indication of an upturn throughout the first half of 2012.” #### New home-appliance subsidies to boost China demand Chinese copper tube production was down 3.4% y-o-y in Q1, due to reduced demand from the manufacture of white goods, and the shorter quarter. It appears that there had been a build-up in stocks of certain home appliances in 2011, and these were not drawn down as expected after the Chinese New Year festival, as demand and general economic growth turned out to be more sluggish than most had been expecting. **National Bureau of Statistics** data for Q1 2012 show that the production of freezers and washing machines in China was down between January and April this year compared to the same period last year, although the production of other goods such as air-conditioning units was up. However, air-conditioning demand has clearly fallen, as inventories have increased from a previous record of 11.94M units at the end of 2011, to around 25M units by mid-March, according to China Household Electrical Appliances Association. Chinese copper tube consumption

We mainly attribute the weaker demand for these specific products to the end of two distinct white goods subsidies in December 2011. The government’s policy of subsidies for white goods being purchased in rural areas expired on 1st December (having been originally introduced in early 2009 in response to the global financial crisis) and the scrappage scheme for home appliances also came to an end on 31st December. However, this year’s slowing economic growth has not gone unremarked by the authorities. While the **180** Chinese government has ruled out introducing a **170** stimulus package along the same lines as the one **160** deployed in late 2008 at the height of the crisis, it is **Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 09 10 11** considering a number of measures aimed at boosting **Data: CRU** the economy in response to weaker than expected indicators. On 16th May, it was announced that the government will introduce a number of new subsidies for energy-efficient products, including RMB26.5B to subsidise the purchase of energy-efficient home appliances. These include air-conditioners, flat panel TVs, refrigerators, washing machines and water heaters, and are expected to directly benefit copper consumption in China. The impact may not be felt until later in 2012 or even next year, however, due to the time it will take to © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 11 of 18 Copper Monitor June 2012 www.crugroup.com filter back upstream to copper tube producers. The high inventories of home appliances will have to be drawn down first before the changes drive higher appliance

production rates which then impact tube demand. It was reported in March that the value of output at **Canghuan Copper Products Co. Ltd** . grew by 32% y-o-y to reach RMB2.9B in 2011. This represents growth of 32% y-o-y. The company, which is owned by the **Golden Dragon Group** , produces high precision tubes for air conditioning, oxygen-free copper tubes for the solar power sector, as well as microelectronic components and radio-frequency cables. In January, Canghuan Copper began an expansion project which will increase its production capacity from 5,000t/y to 100,000t/y, indicating that the market for high-end precision copper products may be more positive than that of more basic semi-fabricated copper products. Q1 alloy RBS production was up slightly y-o-y in China, but down q-o-q in line with typical seasonal patterns. The market appears to be steadier than copper tube at present, and China remains a net importer in this segment which makes it more difficult for an oversupply to occur domestically. #### US awaits construction rebound Output in the US in the first quarter was mixed, with copper tube production down 12.5% y-o-y but alloy RBS output up 3.2% y-o-y to round 62,000t. **Mueller Industries Inc.** reported an annual decrease in net sales for the first quarter, from US$688M in Q1 2011 to US$578M in the same period this year. The company attributed around half of the decline to the quarter being a week shorter than last year’s Q1, and the other half to lower copper prices “which are passed on to customers in reduced selling prices”. Unlike the more wary statements from European companies that we have reported above, Mueller takes a more cautiously optimistic view in its 2012 outlook. The association warned that there could be a copper products surplus in 2015 following the start-up of new projects, adding that processing capacity should not exceed production by more than 15%. CNFA figures indicate that China produced 10.28Mt of copper products in 2011, up by 18% y-o-y. Processing capacity and utilisation rates were estimated at 12Mt/y and 90% at the end of 2011. - **Sindicel** , an association for the Brazilian non-ferrous metals consumption industry, released figures indicating that Brazil’s semi-fabricated copper product output was down by 2.6% y-o-y, amounting to 396,900t (copper content) in 2011. Wirerod production in 2011 was up by 1.2% y- o-y, whereas brass mill output was down by 10.2% y-o-y. Capacity increases in both the wirerod and brass mill product sectors resulted in utilisation rates falling to 47% and 66%, respectively, in 2011. - China’s **Hengyuan Copper** , based in Shandong province, has begun commercial production from a newly installed 20,000t/y copper pipe line. The company invested RMB380M in the line and expects to invest a further RMB581M to initially add a 10,000t/y copper wire line and then a 170,000t/y low oxygen copper rod and bar line. The project is expected for completion by the end of 2014. - China’s **Xingye Copper International Group** plans to commission its 25,000t/y copper plate and strip project in Zhejiang province by 2014. The company already operates a

copper and copper alloy plate and strip plant. 



- **Aurubis AG** reported that its copper products output reached 327,000t in Q1 2012, down by 14.5% y-o-y.  Production of wirerod reached 179,000t, down by 17% y-o-y, attributed to slow European power grid investment.  In contrast, copper shapes and flat rolled products markets are expected to show robust growth in the coming quarters due to support from the US electronics and electrical, engine cooling and distribution sectors.  However, Aurubis does not expect a pick-up in the Asian market until around Q4 2012, adding that demand in Europe will most likely have improved by then. 



- According to preliminary data from the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** , Japan’s April shipments of rolled copper declined by 8.1% y-o-y, to 64,914t. The fall in production was attributed to poor demand from the electronics sector, despite robust consumption by the automotive industry.  Nevertheless, shipments of rolled copper increased 3.2% m-o-m.

#### Mine Production 



- On 28<sup>th</sup> May, the government of President Ollanta Humala in Peru was forced to suspend freedom of assembly rights in order to break up protests and roadblocks surrounding **Xstrata** ’s **Tintaya** mine and **Antapaccay** project.  Protesters are campaigning against alleged environmental pollution from the mine and are demanding that Xstrata’s pays the local government a greater share of its profits.  During the week-long protest, two people were killed and around 50 were injured.  Xstrata reported that operations are proceeding as normal, with good stocks of concentrate at its port ready for shipment.  Production is currently being phased out at the 120,000t/y Tintaya copper mine, with the neighbouring 160,000t/y copper-inconcentrate Antapaccay project set to commence production in August 2012. 



- According to senior officials in the **Indonesian government** , a 20% duty tax on exports of metal ores will apply in the region from 6<sup>th</sup> May.  The move aims to encourage investment in ore processing facilities which would add value to exports and boost domestic industry.  Companies which hold Contracts of Work (COW) agreements, including **Freeport-McMoRan** , **Vale** and **Newmont** will be exempt from this new regulation; however, the government has expressed interest in renegotiating the COW agreements. 



- On 25<sup>th</sup> May, **Diego Hernandez** , the CEO of Chile’s mining company **Codelco** , announced his resignation after taking on the role in 2010.  He will be replaced by **Thomas Keller** , the current CFO of the company.  According to company sources, Hernandez’s departure was linked to differences with Codelco’s board and is unrelated to the ongoing dispute over Codelco’s alleged option to acquire 49% of **Anglo American Sur** .  State-owned Codelco is the world’s largest copper minin

g company, having produced in excess of 1.8Mt of contained copper in 2011. 



- On 23<sup>rd</sup> May, it was reported that **Codelco** and **Anglo American** had agreed to begin out-ofcourt talks and suspend their respective litigation proceedings over the long-standing dispute over Codelco’s claim to a 49% share of Anglo American’s Chilean subsidiary **Anglo American Sur (AAS).** The two companies have been locked in a continuing fierce legal battle since last October when Codelco announced its intention to exercise its option to acquire a stake in AAS. The break in legal proceedings is set to last until 22<sup>nd</sup> June. 



- On 22<sup>nd</sup> May, commodities trader **Glencore** announced that it has increased its indirect equity interest in the **Mutanda** copper mine in the DR Congo to 60% in deals worth US$480M.  The company paid US$340M for a further 24.49% stake in **Samref Overseas** , the majority holding company of the mine, increasing its overall ownership in the company to 74.9%, as well as a further 1% stake in another holding company, **Samref Congo** .  The shares were purchased from **High Grade Minerals** ( **HGM** ) and **Groupe Branzo** , although their ownership details remain undisclosed.  Glencore also paid off US$140M of outstanding shareholder debts.  The acquisition of Mutada is part of the company’s long term plan to merge the mine with the nearby **Kansuki** project, which would cumulatively produce 160,000t/y of contained copper.  Glencore

According to the contract workers’ union at Escondida, the mine operator is currently reviewing the protesters’ demands.

#### Exploration and Development 



-

The board of directors of **First Quantum Minerals** has approved the construction of the **Sentinel** copper project in Zambia after agreeing an electricity tariff level with Zambia’s stateowned electricity supplier, **Zesco** , on mutually agreeable terms.  An NI 43-101 technical report on the Sentinel project, released by GQM on 9<sup>th</sup> May, stated that talks with Zesco “confirm that power costs will actually be $0.075kWh”. Just prior to this, First Quantum announced that it would refuse to begin construction of the project unless a power agreement was reached.  Upon commissioning, the Sentinel Project will commence production at a rate of 150,000t/y of copperin-concentrate, before gradually increasing output to 300,000t/y or more. 



- On May 8<sup>th</sup> , it was announced that the regional environmental commission in the Chile’s Patagonian region of Aysen has approved the construction of the 640 MW **Cuervo** 

**hydroelectric plant** .  The power plant is part of the US$3.6B **Energia Austral** project, a jointventure between **Xstrata** and energy retailer **Origin Energy** , which includes the construction of three power plants ( **Cuervo** , **Blanco** and **Condor** ) and a transmission lines.  The approval came amid some public concern over the project’s environmental impact.  Similar concerns have been voiced over several other planned hydroelectric plants in the region.  In particular, the US$3B, 2,750MW **HydroAysen** project has faced fierce local opposition that has delayed construction for a year.  Estimates suggest that Chile needs to double its current power generation capacity of 17,000MW to keep up with the rising consumption driven by high growth rates in the economy.

The US$60M project will increase the concentrator’s capacity from 68,000t/d to 77,000t/d.  Last year, the mine produced approximately 66,000t of copper-in-concentrate.  The project is expected to be completed in early 2013. 



- On 7<sup>th</sup> May, **Imperial Metals** announced that its **Red Chris** copper-gold project in British Columbia was granted a mining permit.  The project has already received provincial and federal environmental permits between 2005 and 2006.  The mine pr

oject is expected to be commissioned in 2014 and will boast a copper-in-concentrate production capacity of 33,000t/y over a 28-year mine life. 

#### Smelting and Refining 



- **Rio Tinto Kennecott** ’s smelter-refinery in Utah has been shut down for 24 days, beginning 30<sup>th</sup> April, as part of its bi-annual maintenance schedule.  The timing of the maintenance was set to take advantage of the mining of higher grade ore at the Bingham Canyon mine, which will result in higher deliveries of concentrate to the smelter in H2 2012. In 2011, the smelter-refinery produced around 215,000 of copper cathode.
